CDBG - Public Facilities Program (PF)

Content_Area1

​​​​​​​​​​​​​​Program Overview

​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​Public Facilities (PDF) funds help support infrastructure and facility projects for communities. Grants are awarded to units of general local government and are limited to projects that meet a CDBG National Objective, including:

  • addressing the needs of and primarily serving individuals with a low- to moderate-income (LMI) status;
  • eliminating slum or blighted conditions; or
  • addressing an urgent local need.

Examples of eligible projects include construction, expansion, or improvement of:

  • streets/roadways
  • water, sanitary sewer and storm sewer system improvements
  • sidewalks
  • community centers
  • senior centers
  • libraries
  • fire stations
  • homeless shelters

Application Process

​How to Apply

CDBG-PF funds are awarded through an annual competitive process. Application materials and submission instructions should be carefully reviewed prior to applying for CDBG-PF funds.

Review Process

For each Grant Application received on or before the Application Submission Deadline, DOA reviews, scores, and​ ranks the Applications based on a pre-approved list of scoring criteria. Successful Applications must meet a CDBG National Objective (in accordance with HUD program regulations). Applications that earn enough points in the review process will be awarded State CDBG-PF funds.

Award Process

Communities with successful applications (that have met the threshold requirements for funding) are announced and each community receives an award letter which documents the next steps required to accept & execute a Grant Agreement (i.e. contract) with the State of Wisconsin. 

Next Steps & Requirements​

Upon award, community grant administrators are required to attend​ CDBG Implementation Training.

Application Submission

The 2027 CDBG-PF applications due date is to be announced. Typically applications are due in mid-May each year.

INCOME SURVEY NOTICE: Applicants seeking to qualify a project using income survey data to verify that the project will meet the low- and moderate-income (LMI) National Objective must already have a DEHCR-certified Income Survey Packet or must submit a completed Income Survey Packet to DEHCR no later than February 15th* of the year they are applying, unless another due date is specified in the application materials. Late submissions will not be considered. Please refer to the Income Survey Guide on the CDBG Resources and Trainings page for more information and income survey requirements.

*When February 15th falls on a weekend, the Income Survey Packet deadline is extended to the following Monday.
